memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and the livestock that were with him in the ark, and he sent a wind over the earth, and the waters receded. - Gen 8:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After a hundred and fifty long days on an endless sea, we come to the hinge of the whole story, and it turns on three beautiful words: "But God remembered." This does not mean God had forgotten Noah, as if He had been distracted and suddenly recalled the little ark floating out there. In Scripture, when God "remembers," it means He acts on His covenant love - He moves to keep His promise and to help His people.

Imagine Noah's long wait - no land in sight, no word from heaven, just water and waiting, day after day. Perhaps he wondered if he had been forgotten. Then God remembered, and everything began to change. The wind blew, the waters receded, and rescue was underway.

There are seasons in our own lives when it feels as if God has forgotten us - long stretches of waiting when nothing seems to move and heaven seems silent. But God never forgets His own. He remembered Noah, He remembered Hannah in her sorrow, He remembered His covenant again and again. And He remembers you.

The dying thief cried, "Jesus, remember me," and the Lord did (Luke 23:42-43). If you feel forgotten today, take heart - the God of the ark remembers you with covenant love. His remembering is never too late, and it always leads to His saving action on your behalf.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you ever feel as though God has forgotten you?
- How does it comfort you to know that God "remembers" His people with saving love?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that You never forget Your own. In my long seasons of waiting, remember me with Your covenant love, and move on my behalf in Your perfect time.
